The Scrum Master has responsibilities toward each of the team members, as detailed below, in order to maximize effectiveness of the Scrum team.

Responsibilities to the Scrum Team

  1. Make sure the team adheres to Scrum theory, practices and rules
    Responsible for verifying the team members employ an iterative and incremental approach to optimize predictability and control risk. This requires the Scrum Master to guide the team in transparency, inspection and adaptation.
  2. Facilitate Scrum Team interactions to achieve maximum value
    Responsible for making sure stakeholders understand which interactions with the Scrum team are useful and which are not, guiding everyone to adapt their interactions as appropriate.
  3. Host and facilitate all events as requested or needed
    Responsible for hosting and/or facilitating all key Scrum ceremonies while remaining a neutral party. The ceremonies include sprint planning, daily Scrum, sprint review and sprint retrospective. The Scrum Master's goal is to promote collaboration, pursue synergies, and provide clear boundaries when needed.

Responsibilities to the Product Owner

  1. Coach the Product Owner
    Responsible for guiding the Product Owner in creating clear and concise work items, maintaining and organizing work items, creating acceptance criteria and avoiding technical debt. Additionally, supports the Product Owner in learning and understanding techniques and principles of product management in an empirical environment. Ultimately, helping the Product Owner find the right balance between responsibilities toward the team and those toward the stakeholders.
  2. Embrace and enable change
    Responsible for educating all parties, particularly when conflict arises, on Agile practices and work with those parties (e.g. management, HR, finance) to implement the necessary organizational changes.

Responsibilities to the Development Team

  1. Coach the team to self-organize and operate in a cross-functional manner
    Responsible for explaining expected and acceptable behaviors, consequences of not being self-organized, and benefits of working outside business titles.
  2. Remove impediments impacting team progress
    Responsible for supporting the Development Team in the identification and removal of anything that produces waste or causes delays in delivery (impediments). The extent of the Scrum Master's involvement in removing impediments will depend on the maturity of the team and the extent of the impediment. Ideally, the Scrum Master should be aware of all impediments and remove them when the Development Team is unable to do so.
  3. Shield the team from interruptions
    Responsible for shielding the team from outside distractions that have the potential to interfere with their work. This includes monitoring interactions and minimizing them as needed to keep the team on track, typically by helping everyone both in- and outside the team understand these interactions and their impact on the team. If necessary, Scrum Master may suggest that the team create a work item buffer with a small number of story points to be added to the next sprint to account for the time consumed by these interruptions in order to make the impact of these interruptions visible and quantifiable.
